description: Visualizing Bidirectional A* pathfinding on New York (SoHo)
ig_caption:
Bidirectional A* on Real Maps: The Ultimate Pathfinding Algorithm — how autonomous vehicles and routing AI calculate optimal routes in milliseconds ⚡

👀 In this Amsterdam (Jordaan) demo, we run Bidirectional A* from BOTH ends:
1) Forward search: start → goal using f(n)=g(n)+h(n)
2) Backward search: goal → start using g(n)+h’(n)
3) Stop early: when the frontiers overlap (or the best combined cost is guaranteed)
4) Reconstruct: connect the meeting node paths into the optimal route

🧠 Why it’s faster than classic A*:
- A* expands nodes in “best-first” waves, but Bidirectional A* splits the work.
- With consistent heuristics, the meeting condition can dramatically reduce explored area.
- On road grids/graph maps (GPS-like), this often means fewer expansions before the optimal path is proven.

✅ Takeaway: Bidirectional A* is a graph-search strategy that cuts search space by meeting in the middle—great for routing on real networks.

🤔 Debate: In your experience, does bidirectional search win more on dense city grids or sparse road networks?
